opening.argument: The speakers are seated on a summit stage, discussing institutional investors, regulatory conditions, and the future of blockchain assets. The institutional perspective concerns whether large asset owners will embrace the asset class; the tokenization forecast even acknowledges that some efforts will not succeed. These are industry and policy judgments, not a specific investment offered to viewers. The call for a letter, email, or phone call concerns influencing an elected representative's vote, not sending money or credentials. References to adoption and possible future assets do not establish a financial solicitation when the concrete audience action is political engagement.

citations.quote: I'll speak from the institutional investor perspective, Sovereign Wealth Funds, the folks I speak to, like yourself, some state treasurers, large asset owners, insurance pools, getting them over the hump of embracing this asset class
A lot of it's going to be nonsense. But some of it's going to stick.
A single letter, a single email, a single phone call can be enough to switch a vote
